observation.visible_scene: Nighttime view across a dark street of a single-story house heavily decorated with Christmas lights: white icicle lights trace the roofline, two star outlines and Santa figures sit on the roof, the garage door glows pink, and the front yard is packed with lighted props (a white wire reindeer, striped candy-cane poles, gingerbread houses, snowmen, nutcracker figures, small lit trees, a round multicolor 'wheel' light, and a green-lit tree at the far left).
visible_changes: Camera performs a slow lateral drive-by translation: comparing frame 1 to frame 41, the foreground striped candy-cane pole moves from ~x=635 to ~x=815 and the mid-ground white reindeer from ~x=395 to ~x=575 (both rightward), while the roofline stars stay nearly fixed (left star ~x=340→345, right star ~x=695→705). This near-vs-far shift gradient is parallax, not object motion.

As a result of that translation the framing slides leftward: the far-left green light-tree and the candy-striped human figures, partly cut off at the start, become fully visible, while the right-edge snowman present in frame 1 leaves the frame by frame 41.

The light display animates continuously and synchronously: the small central tree cycles between green, red and white across frames; the round multicolor 'wheel' light changes its color pattern frame to frame; the nutcracker and gingerbread-house lights flicker through different colors; the pink glow on the garage door pulses in intensity; the icicle lights twinkle.

These color changes are independent of the camera shift: e.g., between consecutive frames the same reindeer outline stays white while the central tree flips color, confirming two separate processes (camera motion + light animation).
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the camera keeps translating after frame 41 or reverses, and the full extent of the display beyond the cropped left/right edges.
The audio/music track that the synchronized lights are presumably following.
The cause of the color cycling (controller program) and any state before frame 1 or after frame 41.
uncertain_details: Exact direction of the camera translation is inferred from the parallax gradient (near objects drifting right relative to the fixed roofline); a pure pan cannot explain the differential motion.
Whether the round 'wheel' light physically rotates or only recolors in place is not resolvable from these samples.
Minor frame-to-frame jitter of the whole image is present but too small to distinguish from intentional camera motion.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
